newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb patent in interference proceeding.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb patent in interference proceeding.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp said Wednesday one of it patents is involved in an interference proceeding by the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office with a patent application from Plant Genetics Systems N.V.
The interference proceeding is aimed at determining patent rights for a herbicide-resistant corn product, based upon technology claims.
Plant Genetics is an affiliate of AgrEvo GmbH of Germany, which is a unit of a joint venture between Hoechst AG and Schering AG.

DeKalb said the proceeding involves its product patent 5,550,318, which covers genetically altered corn that is resistant to glufosinate herbicide. DeKalb said this patent was issued in August 1996 by the U.S. Patent Office with "full knowledge" of the subject matter of Plant Genetic's patent application.

DeKalb previously sued AgrEvo over the disputed patent claims. Earlier this year, AgrEvo obtained a stay in that case on the basis that the U.S. Patent Office might declare an interference proceeding.
DeKalb said no determination has been made yet regarding to patent rights between it and AgrEvo.

" ...(T)he declaration (of the interference proceeding) does not determine the validity or enforceability of DeKalb's product patent position regarding corn that is resistant to glufosinate herbicides such as AgrEvo's Liberty herbicide, nor does the declaration in any way support the claims of AgrEvo's patent application," Bruce Bickner, DeKalb chairman, said in a statement.
DeKalb has royalty-bearing agreements with approximately 100 seed companies licensing the sale of glufosinate-resistant corn. These agreements are not affected by the proceeding.
